fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Clear vegetation along the access drive edges to maintain an open travel width for emergency vehicles.
• Trim dense vegetation that may reduce visibility of the detached structure from the access drive.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure for responder movement on foot.
• Mark or identify which access point provides the most direct route to the main residence for arriving responders.
• Post the secondary access point address or identifier at the road to avoid responder confusion between multiple entry points.
• Keep at least one parking area clear of vehicles to provide a staging area for emergency equipment.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to approach and move around it.
• Identify the turnaround limitation to arriving crews by marking a designated pull-forward or pull-aside area for fire or EMS vehicles.
• Keep all gates on the property unlocked or fitted with a lock box accessible to emergency responders.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Along Driveway; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure's exterior walls.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep it clear for vehicle access.
• Clear dead leaves, twigs, and dry plant material that has collected under and around the scattered trees closest to the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs near the structure so they are not touching each other or the building.
• Keep the ground beneath tree clusters near the structure clear of dry grass and dead plant debris.
• Trim low-hanging branches on trees near the structure so flames cannot climb from ground-level plants up into the tree canopy.
• Remove dead wood and dry material from the vegetation growing along the driveway edges.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging vegetation to allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
